title: Temporal credit, GAE and the PPO clipped objective
outcome: Compute temporal advantages with correct episode boundaries and inspect PPO clipping for both positive and negative advantages.

exercises.title: Remove the trace
exercises.hint: No later residual receives positive trace weight.
exercises.answer: This isolates the one-step residual calculation and its terminal mask.

exercises.title: Terminate the first step
exercises.task: Mark both steps terminal in the arithmetic helper.
exercises.expected: The first result is 0.5 and does not inherit the second residual.
exercises.hint: A terminal boundary cuts both bootstrap and trace.
exercises.answer: The array illustrates boundary behavior; separate episodes should otherwise be processed with explicit episode structure.

exercises.title: Positive advantage outside the interval
exercises.task: Use ratio 1.5 and advantage 1 with epsilon 0.2.
exercises.hint: Take the minimum of the two products.
exercises.answer: The surrogate stops rewarding that favorable increase beyond the upper boundary.

exercises.title: Negative advantage outside the interval
exercises.answer: The bad-direction probability increase still receives its larger penalty.

exercises.title: Check an unobserved action
exercises.task: Compare the two policies in case B.
exercises.expected: Their sampled terms agree while global KL differs.
exercises.hint: Only action 0 appears in the hypothetical sampled batch.
exercises.answer: Clipping a finite sampled objective cannot by itself bound every unobserved action probability or full-distribution divergence.

exercises.title: Freeze rollout quantities
exercises.task: Explain which tensors should be detached during policy optimization.
exercises.expected: Stored old log probabilities and computed advantages are fixed.
exercises.hint: The old collector and reference policy have different roles.
exercises.answer: Gradients through old probabilities or an unintended baseline optimize another objective and can destroy the interpretation of the ratio estimator.
